chapters.title: Chapter 1: Linear Algebra and Matrix Computation for Machine Learning
chapters.description: Covers the linear algebra foundations used throughout modern neural networks, with emphasis on matrix operations, complexity, and implementation considerations for large models.
subtopics: Vectors and matrices: operations, shapes and broadcasting
Matrix multiplication (GEMM) and complexity analysis (FLOPs)
BLAS libraries and optimized kernels
Memory layout (row-major vs column-major) and cache effects
Batching, streaming, and tiling strategies for large matrices
Basic notions of numerical precision and rounding errors

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Transformer Architecture and Variants
chapters.description: Detailed description of Transformer blocks and common architectural choices used in modern LLMs, including attention, feed-forward modules, and recent component variants.
subtopics: Self-attention mechanism and scaled dot-product attention
Multi-head attention and key/query/value projections
Position embeddings and rotary positional embeddings (RoPE)
Feed-forward networks (MLP) and gated activations (GLU, SwiGLU)
Normalization layers: LayerNorm and RMSNorm
Residual connections, bias terms and common architectural ablations
Model scaling (width, depth, embedding size) and implications

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Pretraining LLMs — Objectives, Data, and Optimization
chapters.description: Principles behind language model pretraining: objectives, datasets, tokenization and optimization methods used to train large-scale models.
subtopics: Causal language modeling objective and perplexity
Tokenization (BPE, SentencePiece) and vocab considerations
Large pretraining corpora (e.g., C4, WikiText, RedPajama) and data recipes
Optimization algorithms: Adam, AdamW, learning rate schedules
Batching strategies, gradient accumulation, and mixed-precision training
Role of training tokens and the relation between tokens, compute, and performance

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Scaling Laws for Language Models
chapters.description: Empirical scaling laws that relate model size, dataset size (tokens), compute budget, and resulting performance metrics like loss and perplexity.
subtopics: Formulation of model, data, and compute scaling laws (Kaplan, Chinchilla)
Optimal allocation of parameters vs training tokens
Implications of scaling laws for model design and training budgets
Empirical evaluation and limits of scaling predictions
Interpreting equivalence statements across different precision or architectures

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Fundamentals of Quantization
chapters.description: Core principles of quantizing neural networks: floating-point formats, fixed-point representations, quantization maps, and common design choices.
subtopics: Floating point (FP32, FP16, BF16) vs fixed-point representations
Uniform vs non-uniform quantization
Scale and zero-point, symmetric vs asymmetric quantization
Per-tensor and per-channel quantization
Rounding, clipping, and quantization error measures (MSE, max error)
Quantization of activations vs weights and dynamic ranges

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Binary and Ternary Neural Networks
chapters.description: Specialized low-bit networks: theory and practice of binary and ternary weight/activation networks, including training techniques and trade-offs.
subtopics: Binary Neural Networks (BNNs): weight and/or activation binarization
Ternary networks and ternary weight representations {-1,0,+1}
Quantization-aware training (QAT) vs training from scratch
Straight-Through Estimator (STE) and gradient approximations
Scaling factors, channel-wise vs layer-wise scaling (e.g., abs-mean)
Prior works: BinaryConnect, XNOR-Net, Ternary Weight Networks

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Post-Training Quantization Techniques for LLMs
chapters.description: Methods used to quantize large pretrained models after training, their algorithms, benefits, and limitations in the context of LLMs.
subtopics: Motivation for post-training quantization (PTQ)
Per-channel range calibration and activation calibration
Specific PTQ methods for LLMs: GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant and relatives
Quantization-aware linear layers and kernel replacement strategies
Limitations of PTQ for extreme low-bit (2-,1-bit) representations
Trade-offs between accuracy loss and deployment simplicity

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Quantized Training and Optimization Strategies
chapters.description: Training procedures tailored for low-bit models, including objective adjustments, optimizer settings, and gradient handling techniques.
subtopics: Quantization-aware training (QAT) pipelines
Gradient estimation for discrete weights (STE variants) and regularization
Loss scaling and stabilizing techniques for low-precision training
Weight clipping, normalization, and per-layer scaling heuristics
Initialization strategies and warm-up phases for quantized models
Measuring and diagnosing training instability with low-bit parameters

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Model Compression, Sparsity, and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
chapters.description: Overview of compression and conditional computation techniques that reduce compute/memory requirements of LLMs, and their systems implications.
subtopics: Pruning: structured and unstructured approaches
Low-rank factorization and knowledge distillation
Sparse representations and sparsity-inducing regularizers
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE): routing, expert capacity, and training
Communication and memory overheads in MoE and large sparse models
Interaction of quantization and sparsity (sparse quantized weights)

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Memory Hierarchy, KV Caches, and Long-Context Inference
chapters.description: How memory architecture and KV caching affect inference for long sequences and strategies to manage memory footprint at large context lengths.
subtopics: DRAM, SRAM and on-chip memory characteristics (latency, bandwidth, cost)
KV cache mechanics in autoregressive decoding
Memory scaling with context length and mitigation techniques
Compression of KV caches and activation quantization
Implications for latency and throughput when increasing context length
Design trade-offs for on-device and server-side inference

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Hardware, Energy Models, and Accelerator Considerations
chapters.description: Describes hardware aspects that determine runtime performance and energy consumption for different numeric precisions and compute patterns.
subtopics: ASICs, GPUs, TPUs and domain-specific accelerators: architectural overview
Energy cost models of arithmetic operations (ADD, MUL) and memory access
Memory transfer costs: DRAM-to-SRAM and off-chip bandwidth implications
Custom hardware concepts (e.g., systolic arrays, LPUs) and design trade-offs
Impacts of integer vs floating-point arithmetic on energy and speed
Methodologies to estimate and compare energy consumption across designs

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Inference Kernels, Libraries and Deployment Frameworks
chapters.description: Common software components and kernel implementations used for efficient LLM inference and deployment.
subtopics: High-performance inference libraries (FasterTransformer, cuBLAS, oneDNN)
Quantized kernel implementations (INT8, 2-bit kernels, ladder-style kernels)
Model serving frameworks and high-throughput runtimes (vLLM, Triton)
Lightweight inference runtimes (llama.cpp) and edge deployment patterns
Parallelism strategies: data, model, and pipeline parallelism (GPipe)
Benchmarking practices: measuring latency, throughput, and memory usage

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Evaluation Metrics, Benchmarks and Methodology for LLMs
chapters.description: Standard evaluation metrics and benchmark tasks for LLMs, along with best practices for fair comparisons and reporting.
subtopics: Perplexity and validation loss: interpretation and calculation
Zero-shot, few-shot and fine-tuned evaluation paradigms
Common benchmark suites and datasets: ARC, Hellaswag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ, LAMBADA, SciQ
Evaluation harnesses and toolkits (lm-evaluation-harness)
Reporting metrics: accuracy, normalized scores, average across tasks
Statistical significance, reproducibility, and common pitfalls

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Mathematical Tools for Quantization and Error Analysis
chapters.description: Mathematical techniques for reasoning about quantization functions, scaling rules, and analysis of discretization error.
subtopics: Norms and measures (L1, L2, max, mean absolute value)
Scaling heuristics (mean-abs scaling, RMS scaling, max-based scaling)
Rounding functions and clipping operators: properties and bias
Quantization noise models and variance analysis
Bias-variance trade-offs introduced by quantization
Per-layer and per-channel error propagation in deep networks

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Throughput, Latency, and Energy Measurement Methodology
chapters.description: Practical methods to measure and report system-level performance metrics of LLMs, including experimental setups and normalization.
subtopics: Definitions: throughput (tokens/sec), latency (time per token), memory footprint
Benchmarking setups: sequence length, batch size, hardware configuration
Using pipeline/model parallelism during measurement
Measuring energy: arithmetic-only estimates vs end-to-end measurements
Comparative reporting and normalization across precisions and implementations
Interpreting trade-offs: Pareto efficiency in latency, memory and accuracy
